plan_evidence.code_changes: Kernel _hardswish_stream only: split the single masked streaming loop into (1) a hot loop over the statically-truncated range [pid*BLOCK, full) where full=(N//step)*step, using unmasked tl.load/tl.store on contiguous bursts, and (2) exactly one trailing masked tile at offset = full + pid*BLOCK + lane with predicate offset<N. Host geometry, BLOCK=4096, the num_vectorcore cap, fp32 compute and the cached integer-address launch are byte-identical.
plan_evidence.hypothesis: The large-input deficit comes from per-element masking in the streaming loop, which prevents the load/store from lowering to full unmasked contiguous DMA bursts, rather than from tile size (tile size is UB-capped: 8192 fp32 elements needs 256 KB against 192 KB available with multi-buffering). Removing the predicate from all full tiles should cut the ~0.75 us per-iteration exposed cost and raise timing-3/7 from 0.098/0.101 ms toward the 1.0 speedup band; small workloads keep grid=1..few so they should move only marginally.

expected_effect.mechanism: Every hot-loop transfer becomes a full unmasked contiguous DMA burst instead of a predicated one, removing per-element predicate handling and the possible non-contiguous fallback that exposes ~0.75 us of serialized latency per 4096-element tile.

plan_evidence.strategy: Cut per-call host overhead in the small-workload regime
plan_evidence.code_changes: Device kernel unchanged. Host path flattened to a single frame: the _strict_empty_like/torch.empty(tuple(shape), device, dtype) call becomes a module-level torch.empty_like alias, _strict_contiguous inlined to an is_contiguous test plus _strict_clone, the plan closure removed and replaced by a module-level flat plan list (_FAST) holding dtype/n/device/launcher/grid/block/fn/packed/stream-getter, and _build now returns that plan instead of a closure so run() calls the C launcher directly with no intermediate Python frame. Stream is still re-read every call.
plan_evidence.hypothesis: The small/medium workloads (10 of 12 timing cases, all at ~0.030-0.034 ms regardless of n from 1024 to 1M) are bound by per-call host cost, not device time, so trimming Python work and switching to torch.empty_like should reduce each call by ~1-3 us and lift those speedups from ~0.84 toward ~0.90, while the 4096x4096 cases are unaffected (they are tile-count bound on device and their host cost is already overlapped).

expected_effect.mechanism: Removing one Python frame, a tuple(x.shape)/device/dtype reconstruction on every call and the closure indirection cuts the CPU-side cost of each invocation, which is the entire cost of the small-workload regime where the device kernel is only a few microseconds.
